newsitem.title: POLAND: ZLOTY ENDS WEAKER AFTER QUIET DAY, DEPO MKT TIGHT.
newsitem.headline: ZLOTY ENDS WEAKER AFTER QUIET DAY, DEPO MKT TIGHT.

text.p: The zloty closed softer against the basket of currencies as a day of moribund trade gave it little chance of regaining ground lost during an early bout of currency buying by refineries, dealers said.
They said the zloty passively followed dollar/mark changes in Europe, limiting its moves to 10 basis points.

"The market was very quiet today and after the early slump the zloty moved only within a 10 basis point range," one daler at a Polish bank said. The zloty closed at 2.8100/10 to the dollar, down from 2.8007/17 on Friday and at 1.8390/05 to the mark, down from 1.8375/88.

Dealers said refineries were likely to be buying currencies to pay for fuel imports to ease petrol shortages in some parts of country. The zloty was at 1.76/1.70 percent from the trading band centre, weaker than Friday's close at 1.84/1.73 percent.

Dealers said the 1.7 percent from parity rate, which centres the daily trading band, proved to be a firm support for the Polish currency which would require a very strong zloty selling impluse to break.
On the money market overnight rates remained stuck at opening levels of 21.45/21.50 percent even though the National Bank of Poland refrained from draining the market today.

No NBP operation helped tomorrow/next offers inch 0.05 point lower to 21.00/21.45 percent, but dealers said one-day rate were likely to stay above 21 percent tomorrow, especially that the net flow on Tuesday was neutral.

At the primary T-bill sale minimum prices of the benchmark 52-week bill and 13-week T-bills rose 0.01 point to 83.57 and 95.50 respectively while the price of the 26-week paper eased 0.01 point to 91.18. Investors bid for a total of one billion zlotys worth of the bills against a total 650 million offer.
For next week the treasury raised its offer to one billion zlotys. -- Jan Strupczewski +48 22 653 9700
